Alex Lee: Quick thread — ran a hybrid FP8+4bit experiment on long-prefill traffic (32k contexts). Comparing prefill TTFT vs decode TPS under different calibration strategies and KV cache layouts. TL;DR below.
Perf Bot: Job 17755 finished: bench/longprefill/hybrid-quant — summary uploaded to perf dashboard.
Maria Chen: Can you paste the raw numbers? TTFT = time-to-first-token and TPS = tokens/sec, right?
Alex Lee: Correct. Setup: Llama2-13B, attention kernels in FP8, MLP weights in 4-bit (APT-style), KV cache stored compressed as int8 chunks. HW = A100-80GB. Workloads: single-request prefill (cold) vs batched decode (steady).
Jay Patel: Results? :eyes:
Alex Lee: Top-level numbers (baseline = fp16):
```
- Prefill TTFT: baseline 180ms -> hybrid 290ms (~1.6x)
- Decode TPS (steady-state): baseline 750 tok/s -> hybrid 860 tok/s (~1.15x)
- Cold-to-steady handoff: first 4k tokens show big jitter due to per-layer lazy calibration
```
Sasha Ivanov: Oof, prefill regression is pretty large. Is the KV compression/decompress step the hot path?
Alex Lee: Exactly. Trace shows kernel selection picks fast fused FP8 matmuls for decode path (read-heavy), but prefill does large matmuls + kv writes which invoke quantize/dequantize stubs and a per-layer calibration pass on first encounter. Those synchronous calibration ops add latency before the first token. Also compressed-kv layout increases memory bandwidth during prefill writes.
Maria Chen: So online calibration is killing TTFT. Did you try offline calibration tables?
Alex Lee: Yes. Offline calibration (precomputed scale/zero per layer) brings prefill TTFT back near baseline (~1.05x). But caveat: calibration tables increase model footprint ~6-8% and we saw more frequent KV chunk evictions on 32k contexts causing decode jitter in peak loads.
Danielle Ortiz: Any changes to batching heuristics that helped? e.g., aggregate prefill across concurrent requests?
Alex Lee: Cross-request prefill batching helps — we saw TTFT improvement ~20% at medium concurrency by amortizing quantization cost. But it adds queueing ~5-10ms which breaks strict low-latency SLAs. For PLG flows it's okay, but not for hard realtime.
Jay Patel: Could runtime pick policy based on SLA tags? hybrid strategy?
Alex Lee: Yep — we prototyped two knobs:
- `prefill_priority` (direct | batch_when_concurrent)
- `calibration_mode` (offline | lazy-online | disabled)
Lazy-online reduces memory and perf overhead overall but creates cold-start spikes (per-layer sync) = TTFT hiccups.
Perf Bot: Flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/17755/flame — hotspot shows `kv_cache::write::decompress` and `layer::calibrate_once` as top CPU stalls.
Sasha Ivanov: Action items: 1) Add offline calibration tooling to model onboarding (Maria) 2) Implement SLA-aware prefill batcher (Danielle) 3) Add kernel-selection rule: prefer fp16 fused kernels for prefill when ctx > 8k or when `prefill_priority=direct` (Alex). Also add perf regression tests covering long-context KV churn.
Danielle Ortiz: I'll own (2). Scheduling work now. :+1:
Maria Chen: I'll own (1) and add memory-overhead tests to CI.
Alex Lee: I'll prototype the kernel-selection rule and extend the perf harness to record TTFT percentiles and KV eviction stats. Planning a re-run overnight.
